subject: Async tool-call timeouts impacting structured output - carveout/credit request
messages:
From: Abby Powell <abby@cloudinsights.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudinsights.com
Date: Sun, 5 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Structured-output failures during async tool calls (logs attached)

Hi Sofia,

We started a pilot of your private deployment last week and ran into repeated structured-output failures when our pipeline invokes the agent toolchain asynchronously. The model request itself succeeds, but when the service attempts to call our enrichment endpoint (async toolcall) the request sometimes times out and we get a partial / malformed JSON back from Redwood. That behavior has caused two automated downstream jobs to fail overnight and stalled a critical dashboard refresh.

I've attached a small log snippet and the service trace from last night's window (trace-async-toolcall-0805.json). Can you confirm whether this falls under your SLA for generation availability or if tool-calling fallbacks are considered an exception? If it's considered an exception, we need written acknowledgement and a timeline for mitigation—this is preventing us from moving more traffic to production.

We'd also like to understand if Redwood will make the customer eligible for a partial credit for the outage window (roughly 02:10-02:48 UTC on 2028-08-05). Procurement is on copy.

Thanks,
Abby Powell
Head of Platform
Cloud Insights

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Abby Powell <abby@cloudinsights.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Structured-output failures during async tool calls (logs attached)

Hi Abby — thanks for the clear note and the traces. I reviewed the snippet and reproduced the pattern in our test harness: the runtime retries the tool invocation once, then falls back to an internal placeholder which results in truncated structured output. You're right that this leads to malformed JSON for your downstream consumers.

Short answers:
- Under our current hosted SLA language, tool invocation failures and downstream webhook timeouts are treated as operational errors and are eligible for remediation, but they are scoped differently from pure model-generation downtime. For private deployments we include a carveout clause for third-party webhook/toolchain failures to account for customer endpoint availability, but timeouts that occur inside Redwood's agent runtime (retry logic, queue saturation) are on us.
- From the trace you sent, we see a 504 coming from our outbound connection pool after two retries; that is internal and we will accept responsibility.

Proposed next steps:
1) Immediate mitigation: we'll increase the toolcall retry window and add backoff for your cluster tonight; this should reduce the transient truncations.
2) A short term carveout/credit: we can offer a one-time credit for the impacted window (up to 25% of the usage fee for that day) while we implement a longer fix.
3) Long term: we'll ship a runtime patch that improves async toolcall buffering and KV cache resilience within two weeks.

I'll loop in Marissa to confirm the commercial language and Ben for implementation timelines. Can you confirm whether 25% credit would be sufficient while we ship the fix, and whether Cloud Insights needs a formal amendment to the SLA or a scoped carveout statement?

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Abby Powell <abby@cloudinsights.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudinsights.com
Date: Sun, 5 Aug 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Structured-output failures during async tool calls (logs attached)

Hi Abby,

Thanks for the trace and Sofia's diagnosis. From a commercial/legal standpoint, here's a concise approach that keeps both parties protected and minimizes paperwork:

- Scoped carveout language we can add: "The Provider acknowledges that failures originating from Redwood's agent runtime (including internal toolcall retry logic, outbound connection pooling, and queue saturation) are treated as Provider responsibility and are eligible for SLA credits. Failures originating from or caused by Customer-managed tool endpoints or third-party services remain the responsibility of the Customer."

- Credit mechanics: Pro-rate credits against daily usage; for this incident we are prepared to issue a 20% credit for the impacted daily usage. We will also include a one-time operational goodwill credit (USD) of $2,500 to cover your overnight incident response.

- Proof and verification: We'll provide the full runtime trace and a short RCA after the patch. If you require a formal SLA amendment (exhibit), we can provide a two-page amendment referencing RDW-5063 and add it as an addendum to your Master Services Agreement. Alternatively, we can issue a scoped carveout statement signed by Redwood's GC if you prefer an expedited route.

Please confirm which route you prefer: (A) quick carveout statement + credit issued within 5 business days, or (B) formal signed amendment (2–3 weeks to finalize). Also confirm you accept the 20% + $2,500 offer (we can adjust if necessary).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-carveout-statement-v1.docx (attached)

From: Abby Powell <abby@cloudinsights.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudinsights.com
Date: Sun, 5 Aug 2028 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Structured-output failures during async tool calls (logs attached)

Marissa / Sofia — thank you for the quick responses and the proposed remediation. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of items before we proceed:

1) We prefer route (A) — a quick signed carveout statement and credit. Please send the signed carveout PDF and a brief note describing the verification window and how Redwood determined the impacted usage.
2) Can you confirm the estimated go-live for the runtime patch? Two weeks from today is acceptable, but we want to validate scheduling.

If you can send the carveout and the credit confirmation by Wednesday (2028-08-08 COB PT), we will sign and move the cluster to 60% of planned production load next week.

Thanks — appreciate the rapid attention.

— Abby
Head of Platform, Cloud Insights
